retrieval_order: Read governance entrypoints and the current branch-state registry before substantive work or before consulting non-main branches.

For successor/V4 integration work, read successor-integration-index, knowledge-base-system-map, version-crosswalk-v2-v4-clean-sheet, v4-clean-sheet-v2-content-crosswalk and web-client-content-contract before treating current presentation code as source truth.

For current product architecture, read final-recommended-public-catalog, course-product-classification, course-system-situation, live-production-role-map and vnext-143-career-guided-map before reasoning from the 143-ID registry or public pages.
Do not interpret course_inventory.jsonl as a command to publish one standalone learner course per registered identity.
Resolve legacy course IDs through course_id_aliases.jsonl before comparing planned versus built state; preserve historical IDs for lineage.

Identify the intended content container before drafting: public course, Field Skill, module, guide, reference, specialist awareness, advanced Owner Review, research domain, historical variant, or defer/remove.
Resolve relevant CONTENT and COMPETENCY relationships through the matrix JSONL tables and claim support through SUPPORT_EDGE to SOURCE; bibliography presence alone is not support.
Check REVIEW, MEDIA, lineage, qualification and supersession state before proposing publication changes.
Use source-citation-regulatory-provenance for authority/freshness/jurisdiction interpretation and sitewide-instructional-media-map for visual selection/release decisions.
Use audience/employer discovery and job-demand-curriculum-bridge to identify learner problems and competency demand; never treat employment evidence as technical/safety authority.

Consult the all-branch catalog summary and current branch-state registry when investigating lost, replaced, archived or alternate course presentations; historical existence is evidence, not automatic restoration authority.
Represent external-system inputs through the cross-system context contract and prefer pointers/provenance over copying volatile source payloads.

Use the Roadmapdev orchestration binding for consequential research sufficiency, conflict, audit, prioritization or architecture questions; Roadmapdev remains advisory and cannot manufacture Crew Blueprint write/publication authority.
Use Production Atlas for current employer, vendor, market, union and opportunity context; do not duplicate volatile state into static curriculum by default.
For proposed content work, follow Content Pipeline v2; it remains a proposed structural contract until owner acceptance/merge.
Preserve source-system authority and provenance in any derived Crew Blueprint work.

authority_rules.crew_blueprint: canonical for Crew Blueprint curriculum, site state, research matrix and learner-facing publication state
authority_rules.roadmapdev: analytical/intelligence source; recommendations do not become Crew Blueprint truth without accepted Crew Blueprint change
authority_rules.production_atlas: canonical for its current industry, employer, vendor, union, market and opportunity intelligence on its accepted branch
authority_rules.50yearroadmap: canonical for ecosystem governance, relationships and accepted current-state continuity
authority_rules.supabase_roadmap: structured durable state/provenance/current frontier; not a replacement for source-repository canonicality

integrity_expectations: all internal repository paths in this manifest must resolve
matrix references must pass repository validation
cross-system pointers must include repository and canonical ref
cross-system analytical records must preserve source authority, freshness and prohibited inference
volatile external-system data should be referenced rather than copied when possible
course content and evidence lineage must remain distinguishable from analytical recommendations
historical full builds must not be treated as automatically current
research-radar, demand-signal and community-discovery items must remain distinguishable from accepted curriculum claims
non-main branches must not become current truth without an explicit branch-state/owner/governance reason
product classification and successor mapping must not destructively rename or delete historical IDs
specialist/hazardous domains must retain external qualification/authorization boundaries
current V4 and clean-sheet presentation objects must not be treated as final source/citation authority when the canonical graph provides stronger provenance
generated instructional media must preserve evidence, rights, accessibility, review and controlled-specialty boundaries
web-client projections must preserve canonical IDs, support state, authority state, freshness and lineage
